A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SENTINEL research work. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary Sections A–G are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SENTINEL benchmark results, component ablations, training analyses, and qualitative evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark comparisons and supplementary ablations and model-family evaluations.

M1.justification: The candidate sampling, object extraction, detector cross-checking, context-coherent preference construction, iterative contextual bootstrapping, and C-DPO objective are unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use Visual Genome for training-data construction and COCO2014 for the motivation analysis. Evaluation coverage remains Object HalBench, AMBER, HallusionBench, VQAv2, TextVQA, ScienceQA, and MM-Vet, with the same supplementary scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 1 and the appendix experiments. This includes Woodpecker and EOS in Table 6, RLHF-V in Table 16, and GPT-4V in the qualitative comparisons.

E3.justification: Training sample sizes, model configurations, training budgets, evaluation metrics, and decoding settings are retained. Appendix E also retains its separate GPT-4o evaluation protocol and the qualification about comparability with main-text HallusionBench results.

E4.justification: The same analyses examine rewriting, detector selection, uncertain objects, context construction, data scale, ICB, and C-DPO versus standard DPO. Training-dynamics plots and Appendix G case studies are also retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, including the 31.0±0.2 baseline entry in Table 13 and shaded bands in Figures 11–12. Neither version supplies additional seed counts, repeated-run counts, or significance-testing information.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains SENTINEL's Object HalBench response/mention rates of 4.3/2.6 for 7B and 3.3/1.9 for 13B. Section 2.2 corrects a color description without changing the plotted distributions or reported trend.

T1.justification: The DPO and C-DPO formulations, context-cancellation reasoning in Appendix C.3, and metric definitions in Equations 3–5 are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: early sentence-level intervention, in-domain preference learning without human annotation or external rewriting, substantial hallucination reduction, and preservation of general capabilities.

C2.justification: The explanations involving hallucination propagation, contextual coherence, detector uncertainty, distribution mismatch, and training stability remain unchanged. The limitation concerning spatiotemporal information and long-term video reasoning is also retained.

D1.justification: Appendices B–E retain the same processing instructions, hyperparameters, prompt templates, implementation frameworks, and evaluation details. Code, model, and data access statements are unchanged; the NLTK citation substitution does not document a software or procedure change.

R1.justification: The NLTK source cited in Appendix B.1 switches from Loper and Bird's 2002 arXiv paper to Bird's 2006 COLING/ACL publication. This is a limited source substitution. Research positioning is otherwise unchanged; duplicate-reference consolidation and same-arXiv title updates do not introduce new research directions.

P1.justification: v3 makes scattered grammar and typo corrections, standardizes bibliography text, and changes appendix cross-reference wording from 'Appendix' to 'Sec.'. Section 2.2 correctly identifies blue as factual and orange as hallucinated in Figure 2a, reversing v1's erroneous description. The document's organization and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 12 and 15 receive small caption edits, and typesetting and reference cleanup cause limited layout reflow. The same figures, tables, and algorithms remain, with unchanged plotted data, axes, legends, and overall display structures.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves a concrete inconsistency by making Section 2.2's curve-color description agree with Figure 2a, helping readers correctly understand the motivating evidence. Small wording, caption, and bibliography fixes also improve presentation. These are limited gains; the method, empirical evidence, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
